briefs.explicit:
MISSION BRIEF S-018
Units: metres, seconds, kilograms. Time starts at t = 0 when every robot leaves its start location.

Locations (x, y, zone):
- base: (0, 0), outdoor
- solar canopy: (-82, -79), roof
- control room: (-112, -121), indoor
- loading dock: (141, 145), outdoor
- east fence: (117, -24), outdoor

Robots:
- M1 (mobile_manipulator): starts at base. Drives on the road grid (travel distance = |dx| + |dy|) at 1.5 m/s; can reach outdoor and indoor locations, not roofs. Equipment: cargo carrier (max 5 kg), robotic arm, camera. Endurance: 3540 s, including the return to its start.
- D1 (quadcopter): starts at base. Flies in straight lines at 8.5 m/s; can reach outdoor and roof locations, not indoor ones. Equipment: camera, cargo carrier (max 2 kg). Endurance: 1500 s, including the return to its start.
- D2 (quadcopter): starts at base. Flies in straight lines at 9 m/s; can reach outdoor and roof locations, not indoor ones. Equipment: camera, cargo carrier (max 2 kg), thermal camera. Endurance: 1380 s, including the return to its start.

Tasks:
- T1: Deliver the sensor box (5 kg) to control room. Location: control room. Duration: 30 s. Needs: cargo carrier (payload 5 kg).
- T2: Tighten the valve at east fence. Location: east fence. Duration: 150 s. Needs: robotic arm.
- T3: Replace the filter cartridge at control room. Location: control room. Duration: 300 s. Needs: robotic arm. Deadline: finished by t = 840 s. Can start only after T1 is finished.
- T4: Deliver the replacement filter (5 kg) to loading dock. Location: loading dock. Duration: 60 s. Needs: cargo carrier (payload 5 kg). Deadline: finished by t = 1200 s.
- T5: Deliver the spare pump (5 kg) to loading dock. Location: loading dock. Duration: 30 s. Needs: cargo carrier (payload 5 kg). Deadline: finished by t = 1140 s.

Rules:
1. Every task is done by exactly one robot. A robot does its tasks one at a time, in the order you list them, travelling between task locations.
2. A robot can only do a task if it has the needed equipment, enough payload capacity, and can reach the task location.
3. A task that must start after another task waits until that task is finished, even if a different robot does it.
4. Each robot must be back at its start location before its endurance runs out.
5. Keep at least 1 quadcopter on standby: it must not be given any task.
6. Every task must be finished by t = 1500 s.

Objective: minimise the finish time of the last task (the makespan).
briefs.informal:
Hi team, here is today's job at the site.

Positions are in metres from the base at (0, 0). Drones fly straight and can't go indoors; ground robots follow the road grid (so they travel |dx| + |dy|) and can't get onto roofs. Everyone leaves their start spot at time zero.

Places: solar canopy (-82, -79, a rooftop); control room (-112, -121, indoors); loading dock (141, 145, outside); east fence (117, -24, outside).

The fleet: M1 is our mobile manipulator at base: gripper arm, camera, room for 5 kg, moves at 1.5 m/s and lasts 59 minutes including getting back. D1 is a quadcopter at base with a camera; it flies at 8.5 m/s, can lift 2 kg, and its battery lasts 25 minutes including the flight home. D2 is a quadcopter at base with a camera and a thermal camera; it flies at 9 m/s, can lift 2 kg, and its battery lasts 23 minutes including the flight home.

Jobs:
(T1) Get the sensor box (5 kg) over to control room - that takes 0.5 minutes on site.
(T2) The valve at east fence needs tightening - that takes 2.5 minutes on site.
(T3) Change the filter at control room - that takes 5 minutes on site but only once the sensor box (T1) has arrived and it has to be finished within the first 14 minutes.
(T4) Get the replacement filter (5 kg) over to loading dock - that takes 1 minute on site and it has to be finished within the first 20 minutes.
(T5) Get the spare pump (5 kg) over to loading dock - that takes 0.5 minutes on site and it has to be finished within the first 19 minutes.

Keep one quadcopter on standby; don't give it any jobs. Everything has to be wrapped up within 25 minutes of the start, and the sooner the last job finishes, the better. Every robot has to make it back to where it started before its battery runs out.
